content.text:
The drawing is a xanthone (9-oxo-xanthene) core with three substituents.

**Left ring:** it carries two adjacent methyl groups. One methyl is on the carbon next to the ring carbon bonded to the ring oxygen (C5, which is the carbon attached to O). The other methyl is on the next carbon over (C6).

**Right ring:** it carries a CH2COOH group on the carbon adjacent to the ring-oxygen-bearing carbon (C4).

**Central ring:** it contains the ring O and a C=O at position 9.

SMILES, written atom by atom:
- Left ring: c1(C)c(C)ccc2c1oc1c(CC(=O)O)cccc1c2=O
- The ring-O carbon is c1, which is bonded to the methyl-bearing carbon c(C) and to O.
- Starting from that methyl-bearing carbon, the ring runs C(CH3), C(CH3), CH, CH, C (bonded to C=O), then C (bonded to O).

Full SMILES: Cc1ccc2c(c1C)oc1c(CC(=O)O)cccc1c2=O

Check on the left ring: c1 (CH3, upper left), c (CH3, upper right, next to the O-bearing carbon), c(O-bearing), c2 (bonded to C=O), then CH, CH. Reading the SMILES as Cc1ccc2c(c1C)o…: the first atom c1 carries a methyl and is the left methyl carbon (C6), followed by CH, CH, then c2 (the carbon bonded to C=O), then c(…) (the O-bearing carbon), which is bonded to c1C (the second methyl carbon) that closes the ring back to the first. This matches the drawing.

The right ring is o-c1c(CC(=O)O)cccc1c2=O, with the CH2COOH carbon adjacent to the O-bearing carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: Cc1ccc2c(c1C)oc1c(CC(=O)O)cccc1c2=O
